title: Learning Neurovascular Codes for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis
abstract: arXiv:2611.31194v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In this paper, we introduce Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations for fMRI generation. We first train a separate EEG encoder to predict each fMRI signal, learning target-specific temporal and spectral features from the same EEG window. After training, we freeze the encoders and project their concatenated hidden features into a shared neurovascular code. Conditioned on this code, stochastic interpolant transforms Gaussian noise into a vector of fMRI signals, allowing different responses to be sampled for the same EEG window. We evaluate our approach on eight public simultaneous EEG-fMRI datasets, including four resting-state and four task-based datasets with 61,646 volume-level pairs. Under within-subject and held-out-subject evaluation, our model improves average Pearson correlation over the strongest encoder baselines by 19.1% and 19.8%, respectively. translated_title: 学习神经血管编码以实现EEG到fMRI的合成
translated_abstract: 在本文中，我们引入“神经血管编码”作为用于fMRI生成的共享EEG表示。我们首先为每个fMRI信号训练一个独立的EEG编码器，从相同的EEG窗口中学习目标特定的时间特征和频谱特征。训练完成后，我们冻结这些编码器，并将它们拼接的隐藏特征投影到一个共享的神经血管编码中。在该编码的条件下，随机插值模型将高斯噪声转换为fMRI信号向量，从而可以为相同的EEG窗口采样出不同的响应。我们在八个公开的同时采集EEG-fMRI数据集上评估了我们的方法，包括四个静息态数据集和四个任务态数据集，共包含61,646个体素级配对。在被试内评估和留出被试评估中，我们的模型相对于最强的编码器基线，平均Pearson相关系数分别提高了19.1%和19.8%。相对于最强的生成器基线的相应提升…
tldr: 该论文提出“神经血管编码”作为EEG与fMRI之间的共享表示，结合目标特定的EEG编码器与条件随机插值生成模型，在八个公开EEG-fMRI数据集上将EEG到fMRI合成的平均Pearson相关性较最强基线提升约20%。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Neurovascular Codes as shared EEG representations, combining target-specific EEG encoders with a conditional stochastic interpolant to improve EEG-to-fMRI synthesis, achieving roughly 20% higher Pearson correlation over the strongest baselines across eight public EEG-fMRI datasets.
